question.description: Focused L0 known-result evaluation grounded in Fisher and Tippett (1928) and Gnedenko (1943). Let X_1,...,X_n be independent rate-one exponential random variables, let M_n=max_i X_i, and let Y_n=M_n-log n. In one authoritative Markdown/LaTeX Theory workspace, derive the exact finite-n CDF of M_n and the support-aware finite-n CDF of Y_n, including the branch below -log n. Then prove pointwise for every real y that P(Y_n <= y) converges to the standard Gumbel CDF exp(-exp(-y)). Make independence, the exponential support, the normalization log n, the fixed-y limiting argument, and the distinction between an exact finite-n law and its asymptotic approximation auditable. Do not replace the maximum by the minimum, omit the finite-n support branch, center by n or log(n-1), reverse a CDF or survival function, claim finite-n equality with the Gumbel law, or generalize the result to arbitrary parent distributions without domain-of-attraction conditions. The required model-authored Python artifact is est_exponential_maximum_gumbel and must implement run_estimator(request) exactly for the frozen closed sample contract. It returns the sample size, maximum, centered maximum, exact finite-n CDF evaluated at that centered value, and standard Gumbel CDF evaluated at that value. Exploratory Python or R may check identities. A separately frozen confirmatory assessment generates independent rate-one exponential samples at several predeclared sample sizes, invokes the exact accepted estimator, verifies the exact finite-n CDF empirically with Monte Carlo uncertainty, and assesses the Gumbel approximation over a preregistered finite grid as n grows. This assessment is distributional implementation evidence, not proof, a universal extreme-value theorem, finite-n Gumbel equality, source replication, novelty, tail extrapolation beyond the frozen grid, or formal proof. Lean formalization is not applicable.

empirical_claims.meaning: Before outcomes, freeze every sample size, evaluation point, seed, replicate count, exact finite-n target, Gumbel target, Monte Carlo precision rule, and joint acceptance decision; generate only independent rate-one exponential observations and invoke the exact accepted estimator for every replicate.
For every frozen sample size and evaluation point, compare the empirical CDF of centered maxima to the exact support-aware finite-n CDF using the preregistered Monte Carlo uncertainty rule.

On the frozen finite evaluation grid, retain exact finite-n and Gumbel CDF errors across increasing sample sizes and assess the preregistered approximation pattern without claiming uniform convergence or finite-n equality.

Retain per-design sample size, evaluation point, replicate count, empirical CDF, exact CDF, Gumbel CDF, Monte Carlo standard error, and estimator invocation failures rather than reporting only a pass Boolean.

The assessment is rate-one exponential distributional implementation evidence only; it is not proof, a universal extreme-value theorem, finite-n Gumbel equality, source replication, novelty, extrapolation beyond the frozen grid, or formal evidence.
